lead.headline: Trump calls Iran war 'effectively over' but keeps the blockade in place
lead.dek: After meeting Qatar's prime minister, he said more strikes don't seem necessary and the U.S. is 'locked and loaded'
body: President Donald Trump said Monday that the war with Iran is "effectively over" militarily, speaking at an unannounced White House briefing after a closed-door meeting with Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who brought a two-day Iranian proposal to end the conflict. Vice President JD Vance sat in on the meeting.

"Taking military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing, but we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes," Trump said. He said the United States would keep "the status quo" at the request of Iran's neighbors: the naval blockade of Iranian ports and the new Task Force Iron Gate, meant to cut trade by land and across the Caspian Sea. The conflict would end "fairly soon," he said.

Tehran rejected the framing. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, called the remarks a distraction and told Washington to stop "manufacturing FAKE NEWS"; Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said attacks and sanctions will not end the war and the two-day plan's conditions "are still on the table." Qatar's prime minister said the talks covered "ways to progress the US-Iran talks."

briefs.headline: Massie forces House vote on 8 Hegseth impeachment articles
briefs.summary: The Kentucky Republican's privileged resolution, filed Monday, must get a floor vote within two legislative days, possibly Wednesday; Hegseth called it a "sham" and holds a rare Pentagon briefing Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court lets Big Bend border wall work resume
briefs.summary: An unsigned four-page order Monday paused Judge Kathleen Cardone's October injunction, finding the government "exceedingly likely to prevail"; only Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson would have denied it.

briefs.headline: Trump questions midterm's honesty a day after accepting it
briefs.summary: "How could the Polls be so wrong???" he posted Monday on Truth Social, asking without evidence whether the election was honest, a day after telling 60 Minutes he accepted the result; Chuck Schumer called the turn predictable.

briefs.headline: Voters shunned pro-war candidates 3 to 1, YouGov poll finds
briefs.summary: 44% said a candidate's support for the Iran war made them less likely to vote for them and 13% more likely, in a poll for Eurasia Group's Institute for Global Affairs on the eve of Nov. 3; 53% want Congress to decide when the war ends.

briefs.headline: Crane collapse at Turkish steel plant kills 17 in Aliaga
briefs.summary: Izmir's governor said an overhead crane fell into an electric arc furnace during maintenance Monday at the Habas works, rupturing a gas line; about 200 workers were in the area, five people were detained and four prosecutors assigned.

briefs.headline: Russia, Ukraine and U.S. open a third Abu Dhabi round
briefs.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meet Vladimir Medinsky and Rustem Umerov on Tuesday in the first three-way talks since Geneva on Feb. 18; security guarantees lead the agenda, and the Kremlin says Europeans will not sit in.

briefs.headline: Saudi Arabia downs 3 Houthi missiles, 2 aimed at Riyadh
briefs.summary: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said a ballistic and a cruise missile were destroyed over the capital Tuesday; Monday's strike on the East-West pipeline caused a "limited fire" and no disruption, the Energy Ministry said.

briefs.headline: Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow office after 33 years
briefs.summary: The paper, whose ex-editor Dmitry Muratov shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize, said authorities "forced our editorial team to cease operations" after fines, a foreign-agent label and the loss of its printing house; Novaya Gazeta Europe carries on abroad.

briefs.headline: Education Department puts $410M price on new school formula
briefs.summary: Blatt's draft, shown to lawmakers Monday, lifts state school aid from $1.41 billion to $1.82 billion, with about $190 million of the increase for special education.

briefs.headline: Delegate demands auditor Hunt resign over nine tax deeds
briefs.summary: Del. Tristan Leavitt said Monday Hunt signed nine deeds for a friend's company past a 120-day deadline; Hunt said on Talkline he acted within his authority.

briefs.headline: PEIA takes 2% premium increase to Beckley hearing tonight
briefs.summary: About 30 people attended Monday's first hearing in Morgantown on a 2% state-employee increase; hearings follow Nov. 12 online and Nov. 17 in Charleston.

briefs.headline: State wins $202M second-year rural health award
briefs.summary: The second-year Rural Health Transformation award, up from $199.5 million, brings West Virginia's two-year total to about $401.6 million, Gov. Morrisey said Monday.

regional.item: A Cabell County judge sentenced Shannon Overstreet, 53, to life without parole Monday for the 2021 killing of his infant daughter.
A CSX train struck and killed a person at Chesterfield Avenue and 57th Street East in Kanawha City just before 6 p.m. Monday, police said.
Wood County's canvass Monday added about 40 of 113 challenged ballots and changed no race; turnout was about 40%, commissioners said.

away.item: HCRS and United Counseling Services' boards approved their merger Nov. 5, forming one agency for Bennington, Windham and Windsor counties.

hotspots.item: Cowen's council unanimously passed first reading Nov. 4 of Connecting Cowen 2026, the town's first comprehensive plan, the Echo reported Monday.
Draft Pender school maps would reassign at least 1,200 elementary students among five Topsail-area schools; a community meeting is Nov. 17 at Topsail High.

briefs.headline: BC Hydro outages near Prince George fall to 4,233
briefs.summary: BC Hydro listed 4,233 central Interior customers still out early Monday, from a 135,000 peak. About 200 spans of wire are down east and north of the city; rural repairs run to late Tuesday at the earliest.

briefs.headline: Final count holds B.C. Conservatives at 64 seats, 2 recounts
briefs.summary: Elections BC closed the final count Monday at 64 Conservatives, 27 NDP and two Greens. Kelowna Centre (43 votes) and Ladysmith-Oceanside (50) go to judicial recounts; applications are due Nov. 16.

briefs.headline: Stellantis signs deal to sell idle Brampton plant to Roshel
briefs.summary: The armoured-vehicle maker gets the plant, idle since 2023, for an undisclosed sum by year-end. Unifor's Lana Payne called it "an underhanded deal"; Minister Melanie Joly said it "does not erase" Stellantis's commitments.

briefs.headline: 15 Wainwright fire soldiers still on ventilators, 9 critical
briefs.summary: Three weeks after the Oct. 17 CFB Wainwright fire killed four soldiers and injured 39, 25 remain in hospital, Global News reported from an Alberta Health Services briefing; Acute Care Alberta confirmed the figures.

briefs.headline: Fossil CO2 emissions set to fall 0.4% in 2026, report finds
briefs.summary: The Global Carbon Project projects 38.2 billion tonnes, with oil down 1.9% on the Iran conflict and clean energy growth; Exeter's Pierre Friedlingstein said a cut driven by shocks "is not a sustainable climate solution."

briefs.headline: ESCAPADE twins swing past Earth, bound for Mars in 2027
briefs.summary: NASA's two spacecraft fired nine-minute burns during flybys Nov. 7 and 9 at 1,000 and 650 miles up, the first powered Earth flybys NASA has used to reach Mars; orbit insertion is set for Sept. 7 and 9, 2027.

briefs.headline: Ice cores trace 1886-1918 arsenic plume to Montana smelter
briefs.summary: Ten Arctic cores show toxins 15 times higher at the peak, tied to the Anaconda mine near Butte: about 11,000 tons of arsenic a year, 50.5 million Americans downwind, the Desert Research Institute said in Nature Sustainability.

briefs.headline: McGill names 30-kg rodent from 34-million-year-old teeth
briefs.summary: Yakamys sirindhornae, known from one molar and one incisor from a Krabi, Thailand, lignite mine, was about twice the mass of any rodent of its era, the team said in Scientific Reports, calling the size a "ballpark figure."

briefs.headline: Anthropic cuts Claude prices 20% as Fable 5.2 tops index
briefs.summary: Tokens fall to $8 and $40 per million from $10 and $50, Anthropic said; independent tester Artificial Analysis scored Fable 5.2 at 65, five ahead of Google's Gemini 4 Carbon, The Decoder reported.

briefs.headline: Households paid 62% of data-centre grid costs, Cornell finds
briefs.summary: Residents on four U.S. grids bore $5.13B of $8.25B in 2025 infrastructure costs while data centres paid $3.12B, researchers said in Nature Energy; AI is 70% to 80% of projected data-centre load by 2030.

briefs.headline: LeCun team's counterfactual rule lifts robot retries to 97%
briefs.summary: Adding the gap between predicted outcomes to the real result let planners hit goals first try in 35% to 69% of simulated events, against 14% to 23% baseline, Brown and NYU researchers said in a preprint given to The Register.

art.caption: The west front of the Supreme Court building from the plaza, its eight-column portico and steps in low sun, after Monday's wall order.

kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers-New River carry no regional line today; a decision on two Nicholas County school closures is due Tuesday.
